concepts: Brand. Demand. Experience.
The Trifecta
Three disciplines that compound when they operate together.
Brand builds confidence, demand creates commercial momentum, and experience delivers on promises. Treating them as a connected loop gives leaders a stronger system than isolated activity reporting.
Which pillar is weakest in your business, and what evidence supports that conclusion?
The Invisible Orchestra
The Operating Model
Growth happens when many visible and invisible contributors work in concert.
Market intelligence, analysts, partners, sales teams, product experts and customer advocates contribute to the brand story. The CMO coordinates the system rather than owning every instrument.
Which important contributor is missing from your current growth rhythm?
Meaning, Momentum and Legacy
Compounding Growth
Marketing is responsible for significance today and durability tomorrow.
Meaning describes why the organization matters. Momentum reflects business progress. Legacy is the accumulated trust and preference that outlast individual campaigns.
Which of these three dimensions do your current dashboards overlook?
Proof before persuasion
Proof & Trust
Evidence reduces perceived buyer risk.
Customer outcomes, implementation detail and credible third-party signals can help buying committees move from interest to confidence. Proof must be relevant and verifiable.
Which claim on your website would a skeptical CFO struggle to verify?
Market memory
Buyer Psychology
Familiarity shapes shortlists before an RFP arrives.
B2B decisions are rarely created in a single interaction. Consistent, useful signals build associations that later influence consideration when a need emerges.
What do you want your brand to be remembered for when buyers are not in-market?
The AI buyer
AI-first Marketing
Software agents increasingly help humans research and compare vendors.
As machine-assisted research grows, companies need structured content, clear product information, evidence, and strong source provenance, alongside human relationships.
Would a buyer or AI assistant be able to trace your top three claims to evidence?
The signal-to-decision loop
Operating Rhythm
Signals only matter when they change an action.
A mature marketing system turns market observations and account insights into decisions, assignments, experiments and learning. Dashboards without decision rights are incomplete.
Which weekly signal should trigger a different decision next week?
AI vocabulary to AI value
Practical AI
AI adoption should be evaluated through outcomes.
Track cycle-time reduction, quality, evidence reliability and commercial contribution rather than treating prompt volume or the number of agents as success metrics.
Which AI improvement could your finance team independently validate?
The cognitive athlete
Future Marketer
The modern marketer needs curiosity and judgment as well as tools.
Critical thinking, financial literacy, experimentation and listening matter more as routine execution becomes easier to automate.
What skill would most improve your judgment if a tool performed your repetitive tasks?
terms: ABM
Account-based marketing focused on selected organizations and buying groups.
Agentic AI
AI capable of performing bounded sequences of tool-supported work under appropriate controls.
AI-first marketing
Designing marketing processes with AI capabilities considered at the outset, rather than added later.
Attribution
A method of assigning contribution to marketing interactions or channels.
Brand equity
The accumulated value of awareness, associations, preference and trust.
Brand health
What people and machines understand and believe about an organization.
Buying committee
The group of people involved in an enterprise purchase decision.
CAC
Customer acquisition cost: the cost to acquire a new customer.
Cognitive athlete
A marketer who combines curiosity, discipline, critical thinking and continuous learning.
Consensus drag
Friction that slows a committee from reaching a purchase decision.
Demand generation
Activities intended to build interest and create opportunities.
Experience design
Planning the end-to-end customer interactions that deliver on a promise.
Human-in-the-loop
A process where a person reviews or approves specified AI decisions.
Marketing OS
An integrated set of routines, data, governance and systems that supports repeatable marketing execution.
Market memory
What buyers remember about a company when they are not actively shopping.
Narrative clarity
How easily people can repeat a company’s positioning without distortion.
Proof architecture
A structured set of evidence supporting claims, outcomes and buyer confidence.
RAG
Retrieval-augmented generation: retrieving approved material to ground model responses.
Signal density
The quantity and usefulness of indicators available for a decision.
Trust architecture
Evidence and governance that make business claims credible and verifiable.
Value proposition
The concrete benefit and difference an offer provides to a buyer.
